newsitem.title: UK: Leeson may gain from Barings collapse film - paper.
newsitem.headline: Leeson may gain from Barings collapse film - paper.

text.p: Nick Leeson, the Singapore-based trader blamed for breaking British blue-blooded bank Barings, could profit from a film of his life story, Friday's Daily Telegraph reported.

The newspaper said Leeson, 30, could have a "more comfortable life" as a result of a deal signed on Thursday when he is released from a Singapore jail where he has now served 18 months of a six-and-a-half year sentence for his part in Barings' downfall.
"It is a substantial deal and should give him a more comfortable life when he gets out if the film is successful," the paper quoted a source close to the negotiations as saying.
But Barings' administrators and liquidators have begun legal steps to ensure Leeson does not profit from his story "Rogue Trader" or a film version of the book.

And bondholders who lost money as a result of the Barings collapse in February 1995 have also vowed to sue if Leeson, who ran up unauthorised derivatives trades totalling 800 million pounds ($1.3 billion), profits from the affair.
Barings was rescued by Dutch financial services giant Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV. REUTER AS ($ = 0.600 British Pounds)
